source: Addison et al. (2021), AJ 162, 292, 'TOI-1431b/MASCARA-5b: A Highly Irradiated Ultra-Hot Jupiter Orbiting One of the Hottest & Brightest Known Exoplanet Host Stars' (doi:10.3847/1538-3881/ac224e; arXiv:2104.12078). TESS 2-minute photometry of Sectors 15 and 16, 15 August to 7 October 2019, the single-scale MAP corrected PDC light curve, fitted with Allesfitter jointly with ground-based transits and radial velocities. Values read from the authors' LaTeX source (arXiv v2): the table of the joint Nested Sampling fit (tab:joint_fit_results), which the paper adopts over the multi-scale MAP PDC and SAP versions and over three other detrendings (the hybrid cubic spline is favoured with ln R = 119). The fit has three phase-curve terms, each a full (peak-to-peak) amplitude counted from mid-transit: the planet's atmospheric modulation (cosine of the fundamental), the star's ellipsoidal distortion (cosine of the first harmonic, 0.0291 +/- 0.0064 ppt) and the star's Doppler beaming (sine of the fundamental, 0.0010 +0.0012/-0.0007 ppt). Only the atmospheric term is the planet's and only it is recorded here. The paper fitted no phase shift, so the atmospheric term peaks at mid-eclipse: a first-order sinusoid whose semi-amplitude is half the printed full amplitude and whose offset is zero by the model, read as amplitude-offset. The table's occultation depth less its nightside flux, 0.127 - 0.049 = 0.078 ppt, is that full amplitude. The brightness temperatures are the paper's own (section 4.2, eq. 3: a blackbody planet against a PHOENIX stellar spectrum through the TESS transmission function), the day side with zero geometric albedo assumed. The band edges are the ones the paper states for this phase curve, 6000-9500 Angstrom.

eclipseDepth.where: tab:joint_fit_results, derived parameters, delta_TESS_occ; undil, Occultation depth (undil.); the diluted row prints the same value

model.equation: With the zero-point of orbital phase at mid-transit, the atmospheric brightness modulation is the cosine of the fundamental frequency with full amplitude A_atmospheric and no phase shift (section 4.1), so the planet's flux falls from the occultation depth at mid-eclipse by A_atmospheric to the nightside flux at mid-transit: F_p = delta_occ + (A_atmospheric / 2) (cos psi - 1), psi counted from mid-eclipse.

semiAmplitude.cell: 0.0785 +0.0073/-0.0077 ppt, printed as the full amplitude; the semi-amplitude is half of it

offsetDegreesEast.cell: not fitted: "Our phase-curve analysis did not consider a possible phase shift in the time of maximum brightness"
offsetDegreesEast.where: section 4.1.2 (Single-scale MAP PDC Photometry), last paragraph

offsetDegrees.cell: not fitted: "we conclude that there is no evidence for a significant phase offset in the planet's atmospheric brightness modulation"
offsetDegrees.where: section 4.1.2 (Single-scale MAP PDC Photometry), last paragraph

notStated: The paper prints no hot-spot offset: its model has none. The zero here is the model's, not a measurement.

The paper's day side assumes zero geometric albedo; it prints that an albedo of 0 to 0.2 gives day-side brightness temperatures of 2700 to 3100 K. The map draws the zero-albedo case, so any reflected starlight is drawn as heat.
The table's nightside flux, 0.049 +0.004/-0.005 ppt, is not an input; the map's night side comes from the occultation depth less the full atmospheric amplitude, 0.0485 ppt.
